Ricci, M. Ricci, A. Rivetti, A. Roy, F. Sarazin, V. Scherini
hep-ph.abstract: POEMMA-Balloon with Radio (PBR) is a hybrid fluorescence and optical Cherenkov telescope that is a pathfinder instrument for a future Probe Of Extreme Multi-Messenger Astrophysics (POEMMA), together with a radio instrument, to be flown on a super pressure balloon in Spring 2028. One of its science objectives is follow up of astrophysical event alerts via signals of tau decays in the atmosphere, sourced by Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. The recent report of the KM3NeT Collaboration's muon event with $ E_{\mu}=120^{+110}_{-60}$ PeV sparked searches for beyond the standard model (BSM) physics explanations. Using a specific, boosted dark matter scenario which together with the KM3NeT observation, sets a scale for the fluence of boosted dark matter in this energy range, we assess the capabilities of PBR to constrain or discover such a source for a boosted dark matter energy spectrum above $\sim 10^8$ GeV. PBR has discovery potential for dark matter energies above $10^9$ GeV, and depending on BSM input parameters, to dark matter energies as low as $1.5\times 10^8$ GeV. While the analysis is focused on one BSM example, the methodology is applicable to any BSM physics that affects tau production in the Earth.

hep-ph.title: Production of excited $Λ_c^+$ baryons through $Λ_b$ hadronic weak decays
hep-ph.author: Kai-Lei Wang, Ya-Mei Cao, Hui-Xiao Duan, Xian-Hui Zhong
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, to establish a more abundant $\Lambda_c$ baryon spectrum, we discuss the production potentials of the excited $\Lambda_c$ baryons through $\Lambda_b$ hadronic weak decays within a constituent quark model. Based on our successful explanations of the existing experimental data for the $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda_c(\pi^-, K^{-}, D^{-}, D^{-}_s, D_s^{*-})$ processes, we further calculate the decay rates of the $\Lambda_b$ baryon into the $1P$-, $1D$-, $2S$-, $3S$-, $2P$-, $1F$-, and $2D$-wave $\Lambda_c$ excited states. It is found that these $\Lambda_c$ excitations have large production rates in the $\Lambda_b$ hadronic weak decay process associated with $\pi^-$ meson emitting, i.e., $\Lambda_b\to \Lambda_c^{*}\pi^-$, their branching fractions can reach up to $\mathcal{O}(10^{-3})$. To search for the higher $3S$-, $2P$-, $1F$-, and $2D$-wave $\Lambda_c$ states, the $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda_c (3S) \pi^-\to D^{*0}p \pi^-$, and $\Lambda_b\to \Lambda_c(2P,2D,1F) \pi^-\to D^{(*)0}p\pi^-$ decays are worth observing in future experiments.

hep-ph.title: Anatomy of RHN DM relic in the vanilla scotogenic neutrino mass model
hep-ph.author: Sujit Kumar Sahoo, Narendra Sahu, Vicky Singh Thounaojam
hep-ph.abstract: The scotogeneic neutrino mass models are very popular choices to generate light neutrino masses via radiative mechanism. In these models, the particles running in the loop are distinguished from the standard model due to an imposed $\mathcal{Z}_2$ symmetry under which the loop particles are odd. Therefore, the lightest particle running in the loop can be a viable dark matter candidate. In this paper, we revisit the minimal scotogenic neutrino mass model and study the anatomy of right handed neutrino (RHN) DM relic, taking into account contributions from self-annihilation, co-annihilation, conversion-driven processes, as well as production via the freeze-in mechanism. We impose the constraints from direct detection and collider searches of DM including anomalous magnetic moment of muon, charged lepton flavor violation and low-energy neutrino oscillation data to show that the lightest RHN can be a viable DM in the mass range: $M_{h}/2\lesssim M_{\rm DM}\lesssim2000 {\rm GeV}$ (thermal DM) and $0.1 ~{\rm GeV}\lesssim M_{\rm DM}\lesssim 1000 {\rm GeV}$ (non-thermal DM), where $M_h$ denotes the Standard Model Higgs mass and $M_{\rm DM}$ is the RHN dark matter mass. We also find the displaced vertex signatures of long lived particles which can be probed at future colliders.

hep-ph.title: Can Mirror Symmetry Challenge Local Realism? Probing Photon Entanglement from Positronium via Compton Scattering
hep-ph.author: Junle Pei, Lina Wu
hep-ph.abstract: This study investigates photon entanglement generated from para-positronium decay by analyzing azimuthal correlations after the double Compton scattering with stationary electrons. We introduce a normalized correlation observable $\mathcal{O}_1 = \cos(2\phi_1 - 2\phi_2)/C_1$ to witness entanglement. In the absence of decoherence, $\langle\mathcal{O}_1\rangle = -1$, corresponding to a maximally entangled Bell state. With decoherence parameterized by $\rho$, the expectation becomes $-(1-\rho)$, allowing direct experimental quantification of coherence loss. A prior symmetry analysis of the Compton scattering process within the quantum field theory (QFT) is provided, which establishes the mirror-symmetric nature of the single-photon angular distribution. We further examine a local hidden-variable theory (LHVT) under the angular-momentum conservation and the rotation invariance. Imposing the mirror symmetry with respect to the plane defined by the photon spin and momentum leads to a non-negative LHVT prediction for $\langle \sin^2\theta_1 \sin^2\theta_2 \cos(2\phi_1-2\phi_2)\rangle$, contradicting the negative QFT prediction value for any $\rho < 1$. Thus, mirror symmetry serves as a novel criterion to exclude LHVT descriptions of the entangled state, whereas without preserving this symmetry, LHVTs can reproduce the correlations.

hep-ph.title: Impact of non-standard neutrino-electron interactions on Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
hep-ph.author: Julien Froustey, Stefano Gariazzo, Jaume Moncho, Sergio Pastor, Ofelia Pisanti
hep-ph.abstract: Neutrino non-standard interactions (NSI) with electrons, predicted in many extended theoretical models of particle physics, are known to alter the picture of neutrino decoupling from the cosmic plasma. We update previous analyses of neutrino decoupling in the presence of NSI with electrons, extending the parameter space and assessing their impact on the primordial light-element abundances produced during Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN). We show that tracking the NSI-induced modifications of the neutrino distributions is necessary to accurately predict the helium-4 abundance, which cannot be derived from a pure $N_{\rm eff}$-driven change. BBN therefore provides additional observables that are complementary to $N_{\rm eff}$. We then derive cosmological constraints on non-universal and flavour-changing NSI parameters, using different dataset combinations, and compare them with bounds from terrestrial experiments. We find that the cosmological limits are significantly less stringent than the terrestrial ones, but they provide an independent probe of neutrino interactions in the early universe.

hep-ph.title: The Residual $288$ in an $E_8\timesωE_8$ Program: Representation Accounting and Physical Matter Interfaces
hep-ph.author: Tejinder P. Singh
hep-ph.abstract: We examine the accounting identity $496=208+288$ in an octonionic $E_8\times\omega E_8$ unification program. The dimensions count selected representation labels, not a closed particle spectrum. In a consistent trinification convention, the quark-doublet labels descend from the $E_6$ adjoint, whereas the lepton-doublet labels descend from the mixed $E_8$ sectors. Their occurrence supplies useful nonabelian multiplicities but does not establish three complete chiral generations. We prove that the stated doublet assignments cannot acquire their Standard-Model hypercharges from a single $E_6$ generator commuting with the full family, colour and weak groups. Separately, a chosen charge-first Clifford benchmark carries three complete families on a $48$-dimensional internal Weyl coefficient space and admits an anomaly-free common family action. We construct explicit subgroup-equivariant lifts of physical scalar currents into $\overline{27}\otimes27=1\oplus78\oplus650$, and show that their nonuniqueness prevents a coupling prediction from normalization alone. The full comparison square contains fundamental family channels; a narrower exclusion applies only to undressed matter bilinears trivial under an independent geometric group. We identify the localization maps, interaction matrix elements, vacuum correlations and kinetic matrices needed to connect the exceptional geometry to physical matter. The geometric interpretation is retained, while generation selection, scalar binding and mass matching remain dynamical problems.

hep-ph.title: Coulomb Effects in Momentum-Space Femtoscopy: A Case Study of the $\bar{K}Ω$ System
hep-ph.author: Pablo Encarnación, Amador García-Lorenzo, Miguel Albaladejo, Albert Feijoo, Juan Nieves, Isaac Vidaña
hep-ph.abstract: We present a momentum-space framework for the consistent treatment of Coulomb interactions in femtoscopic correlation functions based on a modified Vincent--Phatak method that is more amenable to numerical implementation. The formalism provides a practical approach to incorporating Coulomb effects at the short distances relevant for femtoscopy within the Lippmann--Schwinger equation, while preserving a unified treatment of the strong interaction. As an application, we study the $S=-4$ pseudoscalar--baryon decuplet interaction in the $\bar{K}\Omega$ system and present predictions for the singly and doubly negatively charged channels, $\bar{K}^0\Omega^-$ and $K^-\Omega^-$. As an additional validation of the formalism, we have also applied it to the well-studied $pp$ system. We further assess the limitations of the asymptotic wave-function approximation and quantify corrections accounting for the short-distance structure of the interaction potential. We introduce a phenomenological parameter that effectively absorbs contributions from both the finite source size and the off-shell structure of the interaction, the latter being one of the main obstacles to extracting detailed information on hadron--hadron interactions from femtoscopic measurements in a model-independent way.

hep-ph.title: Measuring Ultralight-Axion Coherence with Galaxy Polarization Correlations
hep-ph.author: Yasuo Doi
hep-ph.abstract: Ultralight axion-like particles coupled to photons rotate the linear polarization of distant sources. We propose using the three-dimensional two-point correlation of galaxy polarization-rotation angles to measure not only the amplitude of this birefringence field but also its spatial coherence scale. For a nonrelativistic ALP component with an isotropic Gaussian velocity distribution, the equal-time field correlation has an $e^{-1}$ scale $L_{\rm G}^{\rm phys}=\sqrt{6}/(m_a v_a)$, where $v_a$ is the three-dimensional rms ALP velocity dispersion. A detected turnover in the galaxy-pair correlation therefore measures the characteristic momentum scale $m_a v_a$, while the correlation amplitude constrains $g_{a\gamma}\sqrt{\Omega_a/\Omega_{\rm DM}}$. For a fiducial survey with $10^6$ polarized galaxies over a quarter of the sky to $z=2$ and effective per-galaxy scatter $\sigma_{\rm tot}=10^\circ$, we find $5\sigma$ sensitivity to sub-degree correlated rotations over $m_a(10^{-3}c/v_a)\sim10^{-29}$--$10^{-27}\,{\rm eV}$, with $\sigma[\log_{10}(m_a v_a)]\lesssim0.1$ for detected signals across much of this range. This provides a geometric late-time probe complementary to CMB birefringence and structure-formation constraints.

hep-ph.title: The muon collider: expected physics, technological challenges, and the prospects for reusing the 21 km UNK tunnel
hep-ph.author: L. V. Dudko
hep-ph.abstract: A multi-TeV muon collider is among the main options for the post-LHC energy frontier. Muons radiate about 10^9 times less synchrotron power than electrons of the same energy, so a compact circular collider could combine the energy reach of a 100 TeV-class proton machine with the clean final states of a lepton collider. This review summarizes the expected physics programme, including Higgs couplings and self-coupling, electroweak and top-quark physics, and searches beyond the Standard Model. It also describes the technological challenges: muon production, ionization cooling, rapid acceleration, high-field HTS magnets, the machine-detector interface and the neutrino-flux constraint. None of these technologies has yet been demonstrated at the required performance. Scaling the parameters of the International Muon Collider Collaboration (IMCC), the review examines three ways of reusing the existing 21 km UNK tunnel near Protvino. With the last rapid-cycling synchrotron in the tunnel, the centre-of-mass energy is limited to about 6 TeV. With the collider ring in the tunnel, 11-16 T dipoles give about 14-21 TeV, but the acceleration chain needs a separate 50-73 km tunnel. With both in the tunnel, the reach is about 6-10 TeV at 35-57% of the target luminosity. Non-collider applications of intense muon beams are also discussed.

hep-ph.title: Vector mesons leading-twist longitudinal distribution amplitudes and related semi-leptonic decays within QCD sum rules
hep-ph.author: Wan-Bing Luo, Ru-Meng Pan, Ya-Xiong Wang, Tao Zhong
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, we focus on the light vector meson leading-twist longitudinal distribution amplitudes (DAs) $\phi^\parallel_{2;V}(x,\mu)$ with $V = \rho, K^\ast, \phi$. A new scheme of QCD sum rule research with respect to DA suggested in 2021 by us is adopted. With an improved sum rule formula, the $\xi$-moments $\langle\xi^n\rangle_{2;V}^\parallel$ up to tenth order are calculated. In which, $\langle\xi^2\rangle^\parallel_{2;\rho}=0.225^{+0.013}_{-0.012}$, $\langle\xi^1\rangle^\parallel_{2;K^\ast}=-0.0228^{+0.0042}_{-0.0040}$, $\langle\xi^2\rangle^\parallel_{2;K^\ast}=0.217^{+0.007}_{-0.007}$, $\langle\xi^2\rangle^\parallel_{2;\phi}=0.209^{+0.020}_{-0.020}$, and the corresponding Gegenbauer moments $a^{2;\parallel}_{2;\rho}=0.074^{+0.039}_{-0.036}$, $a^{1;\parallel}_{2;K^\ast}=-0.038^{+0.007}_{-0.007}$, $a^{2;\parallel}_{2;K^\ast}=0.050^{+0.020}_{-0.019}$, $a^{2;\parallel}_{2;\phi}=0.027^{+0.058}_{-0.058}$ at the scale $\mu = 1~{\rm GeV}$, respectively. By fitting those $\langle\xi^n\rangle^\parallel_{2;V}(n = 1,2,\cdots,10)$ with the least squares method, the behaviors of leading-twist longitudinal DAs for $\rho, K^\ast, \phi$ are determined. In addition, we also analyze the impact of incorporating different numbers of $\xi$-moments into the fitting on the stability and reliability of the obtained DAs. Be different from the pion leading-twist DA, we find that the higher-order moments do not significantly change the reconstructed shapes of $\phi^\parallel_{2;V}(x,\mu)$. Further, we recalculate the transition form factors and branching ratios of the $D\to(\rho,K^\ast)$, $D_s\to\phi$ semi-leptonic decay processes.

hep-ph.title: Seesaw Cosmology
hep-ph.author: Nicolás Bernal, Chee Sheng Fong, Óscar Zapata
hep-ph.abstract: We study perturbative reheating in which the inflaton transfers its energy to the Standard Model through right-handed neutrinos (RHNs) responsible for light-neutrino masses via the type-I seesaw mechanism. We refer to the resulting nonstandard thermal history as $seesaw$ $cosmology$. When produced relativistically and sufficiently long lived, the RHNs generate a characteristic sequence of inflaton, relativistic-RHN, nonrelativistic-RHN, and Standard Model radiation domination. We solve the Boltzmann system while retaining the production-time dependence of the nonthermal RHN distribution and its relativistic-to-nonrelativistic transition. The Standard Model temperature rapidly approaches a plateau during inflaton domination and subsequently scales as $a^{-1/4}$ and $a^{-3/8}$ during relativistic- and nonrelativistic-RHN domination, respectively. We investigate the implications of seesaw cosmology for dark-matter production. Direct production through inflaton decays can be enhanced relative to conventional reheating by a factor of order $m_\phi/(2m_N)$, while ultraviolet freeze-in exhibits the critical temperature powers $p = 12$ and $20$, leading to potentially large contributions before the final radiation-dominated era. Seesaw cosmology therefore connects neutrino-mass generation, the pre-BBN thermal history and phenomena such as dark-matter production and baryogenesis.

hep-ph.title: On the nature of fully-charmed four-quark exotic state $X(6900)$ from its photoproduction off nuclei
hep-ph.author: E. Ya. Paryev
hep-ph.abstract: The possibility to study the nature of fully-charmed tetraquark state $X(6900)$ from its inclusive photoproduction off nuclei near the kinematic threshold is investigated within the collision model based on the nuclear spectral function. The model accounts for $X(6900)$ production in direct photon--nucleon interactions as well as three different scenarios for its internal structure: compact tetraquark, molecule of the two hidden-charm $J/\psi$ and $\psi(3770)$ mesons and the mixture of both of them. We calculate within these scenarios the absolute and relative excitation functions on $^{12}$C and $^{184}$W nuclei at near-threshold photon energies of 30--40 GeV, the absolute momentum differential cross sections and ratios of them for the $X(6900)$ meson production off these target nuclei at laboratory polar angles of 0$^{\circ}$--5$^{\circ}$ and for photon energy of 35 GeV as well as the A-dependences of its transparency ratios at photon energy of 35 GeV. We show that these observables reveal a definite sensitivity to the $X(6900)$ intrinsic structure. Therefore, they might be useful for the determination of this structure from the comparison of them with the experimental data from the future experiments at the upcoming experimental facilities, such as the planned electron-ion colliders in the United States and China.

hep-ph.title: Exclusive Determination of $|V_{cb}|$ from Semileptonic Decays $B\to D^{(*)}\ell ν_{\ell}$
hep-ph.author: Xue-Wen Chen, Bo-Yan Cui, Jia-Wei Zhang, Xue-Chen Zhao, Ya-Hui Chen
hep-ph.abstract: We present an updated exclusive determination of the CKM matrix element \(|V_{cb}|\) from the semileptonic decays \(B\to D^{(*)}\ell\bar{\nu}_{\ell}\). Our analysis combines the latest Belle II measurements, updated lattice-QCD calculations of the \(B\to D^{(*)}\) form factors at small hadronic recoil, and correlated large-recoil SCET sum-rule predictions incorporating next-to-leading-order QCD corrections and several power-suppressed contributions. We consider three fit scenarios with progressively enlarged input sets and find that the inclusion of the large-recoil sum-rule constraints substantially reduces the form-factor uncertainties. From the full global fit, we obtain\(|V_{cb}|=(39.18 \pm0.47)\times10^{-3}\). Using the combined lattice-QCD and LCSR fit, we predict \(R(D)=0.3069\pm0.0080,\qquad R(D^*)=0.2548\pm0.0043\), and provide differential decay distributions in the momentum transfer and angular variables for both the muon and tau channels. Comparisons of the individual and correlated predictions for \(R(D)\) and \(R(D^*)\) with the experimental averages reveal a persistent tension. In particular, our theoretical 68\% confidence region shows little overlap with the experimental average. All correlations among the fitted parameters are retained in the uncertainty propagation. Our results therefore provide updated Standard Model benchmarks for tests of lepton-flavor universality. Improved lattice-QCD calculations, sum-rule predictions, and Belle II measurements will be essential for determining whether the remaining discrepancies originate from theoretical systematic uncertainties or from physics beyond the Standard Model.

hep-ph.title: Orbital angular momentum at small $x$ in the large $N_c\&N_f$ limit
hep-ph.author: G. Zardo Becker, Yuri V. Kovchegov, Ming Li, Brandon Manley, Andrey Tarasov
hep-ph.abstract: We extend the small-$x$ analysis of the quark and gluon orbital angular momentum (OAM) distributions in the proton from the large-$N_c$ limit considered in our earlier works to the large-$N_c\&N_f$ limit, in which the numbers of quark colors $N_c$ and flavors $N_f$ are large with their ratio held fixed. Working in the double-logarithmic approximation (DLA), summing powers of $\alpha_s \ln^2(1/x)$ with $\alpha_s$ the strong coupling and $x$ the proton's momentum fraction carried by a parton, we correct the small-$x$ operator expression for the quark OAM distribution suggested earlier in \cite{Kovchegov:2024wjs} and relate both the quark and gluon OAM distributions to the impact-parameter moments of the polarized dipole amplitudes. We derive the large-$N_c\&N_f$ evolution equations for these moment amplitudes in the DLA; these include a new equation for the moment amplitude governing the quark OAM. We then solve these evolution equations numerically together with the helicity evolution for $N_f = 2,3,4,5,6$ and $N_c =3$. We find that, similar to the large-$N_c$ case, the OAM distributions share a common small-$x$ intercept with the helicity distributions, $L_{q+\bar{q}}(x,Q^2) \sim L_G(x,Q^2) \sim \Delta \Sigma (x,Q^2) \sim \Delta G(x,Q^2) \sim \left(\frac{1}{x} \right)^{\alpha_h}$ with the intercept $\alpha_h \approx {3.48 \sqrt{\alpha_s N_c/2\pi}}$ for $N_f = N_c = 3$ (cf.~\cite{Borden:2025ehe}): this result, along with $\alpha_h$ for other values of $N_f \neq 0$ that we studied, is smaller than the intercept of $3.66\sqrt{\alpha_s N_c/2\pi}$ found in the large-$N_c$ limit. We also compute the ratios of the OAM distributions to the helicity parton distribution functions as $x\to 0$, obtaining $L_{q+\bar{q}}(x,Q^2)/\Delta\Sigma(x,Q^2) = -1$ and $L_G(x,Q^2)/\Delta G(x,Q^2) = -2$ at $Q^2=10\, \mathrm{GeV}^2$, with both ratios being independent of $N_f$.

hep-ph.title: Semi-visible Jets from Sneaky Dark Matter
hep-ph.author: Deepak Kar, Christiane Scherb, Pedro Schwaller, Sukanya Sinha
hep-ph.abstract: In this paper, we compare two different ways of generating semi-visible jet signature in non-resonant production mode, and flag the potential advantages of the new generation approach we propose. In addition, we suggest a more efficient matrix element to parton shower matching configuration for this hadronic final state signature. Finally, we perform a reinterpretation study of the ATLAS search for t-channel semi-visible jet production and obtain collider limits on the sneaky DM scenario.

hep-ph.title: Bottom-Charm $[bc]$ Diquark Masses from QCD Laplace Sum-Rules
hep-ph.author: T. de Oliveira, D. Harnett, J. Ho, R.T. Kleiv, Siyuan Li, N. Loewen, A. Palameta, T.G. Steele
hep-ph.abstract: Constituent mass predictions for bottom-charm $[bc]$ color-antitriplet diquarks are generated using QCD Laplace sum rules. We calculate the diquark correlator within the operator product expansion to next-to-leading-order (NLO), including terms proportional to the four- and six-dimensional gluon and six-dimensional quark condensates. Existing analytic expressions for the resulting multi-scale master integrals are insufficient for these calculations, so we utilize numerical $D$-dimensional loop integration techniques. The sum rule analyses stabilize in all four channels yielding constituent masses in GeV of: scalar ($0^+$) $(5.60\pm0.56)$, pseudoscalar ($0^-$) $(6.04\pm0.60)$, axial vector ($1^+$) $(5.60\pm0.56)$ and vector ($1^-$) $(5.99\pm0.60)$. These constituent mass results are discussed in comparison with values used in diquark models of tetraquark hadronic states. We also summarize QCD sum rule predictions for diquark masses for all possible quark-flavor combinations, providing QCD-based criteria for assessing the diquark mass parameters used in constituent diquark models of hadrons.

hep-ph.title: CT25: the new generation of CTEQ-TEA PDFs
hep-ph.author: Alim Ablat, Daniel Adamiak, Aurore Courtoy, Sayipjamal Dulat, Yao Fu, Marco Guzzi, T. J. Hobbs, Joey Huston, Maximiliano Ponce Chavez, Kirtimaan Mohan, Pavel Nadolsky, Tanishq Sharma, Dan Stump, Keping Xie, C.-P. Yuan
hep-ph.abstract: This contribution reviews CT25, a new generation of CTEQ--TEA parton distribution functions (PDFs) for precision QCD. With its first member sets released in 2025, the CT25 family addresses common uses of parton distributions in diverse contexts. We describe the CTEQ--TEA Parton Cloud, an online database of exploratory global fits to precision QCD measurements, from which we select PDF solutions for general- and special-purpose calculations. These solutions are published as complementary error PDF ensembles---the baseline CT25, CT25m, CT25pd, and ensembles with conservative priors---optimized for distinct uses. They implement new approaches to quantifying uncertainties and different treatments of theoretical, parametrization, and nuclear-target uncertainties. In particular, they provide complementary frameworks for exploring PDF uncertainties at large partonic momentum fractions relevant to HL-LHC and EIC studies. Further details will appear in the forthcoming CT25 publication.

hep-ph.title: Field-Induced Weyl-Like Crossings and Longitudinal Magnetoconductivity in Dirac Systems
hep-ph.author: J. L. Acosta Avalo
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the field-induced separation of effective Weyl-like crossings and the associated longitudinal magnetoconductivity in Dirac systems using a finite-temperature quantum electrodynamics response-function approach. Starting from the one-loop photon polarization tensor in a magnetized fermionic medium, we identify a longitudinal electromagnetic mode associated with a nonvanishing pseudoscalar invariant ${\bf E}\cdot{\bf B}$. We use this response to construct an effective low-energy Dirac model in which the two chiral sectors undergo opposite momentum shifts. Within this description, we derive an analytical expression for the longitudinal magnetoconductivity without introducing an independent phenomenological internode relaxation time. The chiral contribution contains an explicit $B^2$ prefactor, while its coefficient depends on the magnetic field and temperature through Landau-level thresholds and Fermi-Dirac occupation factors. The resulting conductivity exhibits a nonmonotonic magnetic-field dependence and an inverse-temperature regime under appropriate conditions. These results provide a connection, within the proposed effective model, between the longitudinal electromagnetic response, field-induced Weyl-like crossings, and longitudinal magnetotransport.

hep-ph.title: Fine-Tuning Small Reasoning Models for Quantum Field Theory
hep-ph.author: Nathaniel S. Woodward, Zhiqi Gao, Yurii Kvasiuk, Kendrick M. Smith, Frederic Sala, Moritz Münchmeyer
hep-ph.abstract: Despite the growing application of large language models (LLMs) to theoretical physics, there has been little academic exploration of how domain-specific physics reasoning ability develops during training. To investigate this, we perform the first academic comparison of reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning for LLMs on verifiable problem-solving tasks in theoretical physics. Because the open-source verifiable training data required to develop such capabilities is scarce, we built a robust data generation pipeline that can both create synthetic problems and make existing human-authored problems suitable for model training. Selecting quantum field theory (QFT) as our primary domain, we generated over 2,500 synthetic problems alongside a curated collection of human-adapted problems sourced from arXiv and standard pedagogical resources. We conduct both reinforcement learning (RL) and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) experiments, benchmarking performance gains as well as generalization to other physics domains. Although both methods improve over the base model on every dataset, SFT gains are concentrated on in-distribution synthetic tasks, while RL generalizes better, outperforming SFT on the human-adapted datasets and TPBench. We perform an extensive analysis of model chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning before and after fine-tuning to understand how reasoning errors evolve during RL and SFT. Finally, we publicly release our data pipeline, verifiable QFT training data, and ~200M tokens of QFT reasoning traces.

hep-ph.title: Agentic AI Detector Co-design and Optimization in Vertically Integrated Differentiable Full Simulations
hep-ph.author: Wonyong Chung, Qibin Liu, Liangyu Wu, Julia Gonski
hep-ph.abstract: We present the first implementation of AI agents into the design and optimization of detectors in high-energy physics experiments via a bi-level optimization framework that vertically integrates detector geometry, front-end digitization, and high-level reconstruction algorithm parameters in differentiable full simulations. Using the example of a dual-readout, segmented crystal EM calorimeter with a baseline resolution of $3\%/\sqrt{E}$, we investigate the capabilities and value propositions of AI agents in the identification and reduction of key detector parameters and in the nonlinear traversal of design space. We find that frontier LLM reasoning-models today, without being given additional experiment-specific context, are able to effectively execute complex workflows and proactively suggest generic but relevant avenues for further study or improvement. Here, we demonstrate an AI agent's ability to find an optimal design point amidst three competing performance criteria, showing that effective integration of agents into the complex workflows of frontier research areas can yield higher performance for key physics goals while reducing labor and compute. This study establishes the foundation for a future demonstration of the first fully AI-designed detector for future scientific facilities.

hep-ph.title: Ultralight dark matter mixed with primordial black holes
hep-ph.author: Xing-Yu Yang
hep-ph.abstract: Dark matter candidates span many orders of magnitude in mass, from ultralight bosonic fields to massive compact objects. In this work, we connect these two extremes by investigating ultralight dark matter (ULDM) mixed with primordial black holes (PBHs). We study mixed ULDM-PBH halos by separating the continuum PBH contribution from the shot-noise fluctuation generated by discrete PBHs. The continuum contribution enters the averaged Schrödinger-Poisson background, while the discreteness contribution is treated as a perturbation that induces ULDM eigenmode transitions and soliton heating. The two contributions have distinct parametric dependencies: continuum effects scale with PBH fraction, whereas discreteness-driven transition rates scale with the product of PBH fraction and individual PBH mass in the perturbative regime. For a fiducial mixed halo with ULDM particle mass $10^{-22}\,\mathrm{eV}$, virial mass of order $10^{10}\,M_{\odot}$, and PBH fraction $1\%$, the continuum PBH component modifies the background density, gravitational potential, and low-lying ULDM eigenvalues only at the sub-percent level. Nevertheless, this percent-level continuum PBH contribution produces a tens-of-percent response in the coherent soliton region, changing the radial mode participation by about $20\%$. For stellar-mass PBHs, the discrete shot-noise fluctuation induces extremely slow ULDM mode transitions, with the fastest low-lying multiplet transition having a timescale of order $10^9\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ for solar-mass PBHs. In this regime, the leading PBH effect is the continuum contribution, while discrete PBH shot noise is dynamically negligible on galactic timescales.

hep-ph.title: Towards anomaly detection searches for new physics signatures including Higgs bosons with weakly supervised machine learning
hep-ph.author: Chi Lung Cheng, Julia Gonski, Julie Khalilieh Romman, Runze Li, Qibin Liu, Benjamin Nachman, Dennis Noll, Liangyu Wu
hep-ph.abstract: The Higgs boson, with its universal coupling to mass, provides a broadly applicable portal to sectors beyond the Standard Model and is therefore a natural anchor for anomaly detection (AD) at collider experiments. The Higgs And X Anomaly Detection (HAXAD) strategy offers a principled approach to searching for such anomalies occurring in association with a Higgs boson by combining machine-learning-based feature embedding, background estimation, and weakly supervised classification. This work extends the previous HAXAD approach towards the level of maturity required for application to recorded collider data. A major addition is the introduction and comparison of two new embedding strategies, which in turn shape the background estimation and classification. In addition, a new inference framework is developed, yielding signal-agnostic and signal-specific cross section limits and thereby completing the statistical machinery needed for future AD analyses built on HAXAD. The set of investigated signal models is also significantly expanded, allowing for the evaluation of sensitivity on a much broader phase space. Improvements to the method increase signal sensitivity with respect to the original method, and when benchmarked against an example cut-based search on the same final state, HAXAD matches or exceeds the best individual cut-based limits for a wide variety of considered signal models. These developments strengthen the case for HAXAD as a viable and compelling AD-based search strategy with novel discovery potential at colliders.

hep-ph.title: Searching for signatures of self-interacting dark matter in halos from full physics simulations: From 3D structure to projected observables
hep-ph.author: Giovanni Y. Ferron, Antonio Ragagnin, Lorenzo Pizzuti, Moritz S. Fischer
hep-ph.abstract: In this work we explore the imprints of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) on the structure of simulated galaxy groups and clusters in view of future optical surveys. We find that both baryonic and projection effects lead to a significant alleviation of the SIDM core-forming behavior on the mass and density profiles, resulting in very small ($\lesssim 5\%$) deviations from standard collisionless dark matter. The opposite trend emerges for our most massive halos, where SIDM tends to significantly enhance the central density instead; we compare those halos with the observed dark matter profiles of two galaxy clusters, MACS J1206 and Abell S1063, finding that SIDM may leave potentially detectable imprints on cluster cores when considering the small observational uncertainty of current kinematic mass measurements. Finally, we find that weak lensing observations provide a promising tool for testing SIDM on cluster scales: in an idealized scenario where systematics are under control, weak lensing shear profiles exhibit up to $\sim 20\%$ level deviations for $M_{200} \gtrsim 10^{13}\ \text{M}_\odot$ halos. Conversely, the projected concentration-mass relation is only slightly modified by our SIDM models. We also discuss the limitiations of our analysis and the impact of the simulation resolution, as well as possible extension of this work. Overall, our results provide a baseline for future SIDM studies: although line-of-sight projection and baryonic effects significantly reduce SIDM imprints on halo mass profiles, weak lensing and kinematic analyses in galaxy clusters may potentially allow for robust detection and constraining of dark matter self-interactions in massive structures from megaparsec down to kiloparsec scales.

hep-ph.title: Evidence for Normal Neutrino Ordering with Combined Atmospheric Neutrino Experiments
hep-ph.author: Miaochen Jin, Carlos A. Argüelles, Pablo Fernández-Menéndez, Iván Martínez-Soler
hep-ph.abstract: We present a combined analysis of the latest publicly available atmospheric neutrino data from Super-Kamiokande including all data-taking stages previous to the gadolinium phase, IceCube-DeepCore, and the six-detection-unit configuration of KM3NeT/ORCA. Our fit uses all event samples simultaneously and treats the systematic uncertainties shared among experiments as fully correlated, while detector-response uncertainties are modeled independently for each experiment. The combined data constrain the atmospheric oscillation parameters to $\Delta m^2_{31} = 2.44^{+0.06}_{-0.04} \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{eV}^2$ and $\sin^2\theta_{23} = 0.52^{+0.03}_{-0.04}$, with a precision of $2.2\%$ and $6.1\%$, respectively, which is competitive with current accelerator-based measurements, and independently constrain the $CP$-violating phase to $\delta_{CP} = 1.30^{+0.24}_{-0.28}~\pi$. Finally, comparing the orderings of the neutrino mass spectrum, we find a preference for the normal ordering with $\Delta\chi^2 = 11.0$; further calibrated with pseudoexperiments, we exclude the inverted ordering at $99.95\%$ confidence level ($3.3\sigma$). In a joint fit including 207 days of JUNO data, we further exclude the inverted ordering at $\Delta \chi^2 = 15.1$, corresponding to $3.9 \sigma$.

hep-ph.title: Sensitivity of calibration-free DESI DR2 BAO--supernova constraints to a distance-duality tilt
hep-ph.author: Mikel Artola, Stéphane Fay, Leandros Perivolaropoulos
hep-ph.abstract: Recent measurements from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) have reported a moderate preference for dynamical dark energy, challenging the $\Lambda$CDM paradigm. Nonetheless, such a trend could reflect a tension between the shape and the offset of the Hubble diagrams predicted by current BAO and Type Ia supernovae (SN) data, which may underpin a possible breakdown of the cosmic distance duality relation linking luminosity distances $D_{\rm L}$ and angular-diameter distances $D_{\rm A}$. We explore this possibility by parametrizing deviations from this relation as $\eta(z)\equiv D_{\rm L}/[{(1+z)}^2D_{\rm A}]=\alpha{(1+z)}^\varepsilon$, and investigate how the preference for a Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) dynamical dark energy is modified once $\varepsilon\neq0$ is allowed. Using DESI DR2 and uncalibrated SN data (Pantheon$+$, DES-Dovekie, Union3, and Union3.1), we find that allowing $\varepsilon$ to vary freely in both $\Lambda$CDM and CPL reduces the CPL preference with respect to $\Lambda$CDM by a larger amount than the addition of spatial curvature $\Omega_k$; only Union3.1 exhibits comparable reductions. We also find that the preference reduction is robust to alternative $\eta(z)$ parametrizations, and that the $\eta(z)$ constraints remain stable under the removal of BAO tracers or low-redshift cutoffs for Pantheon$+$, whereas the DES-Dovekie preference largely disappears once $z<0.1$ SN are removed. In a separate calibrated analysis, illustrative Planck sound-horizon and SH0ES absolute-magnitude priors give $\alpha\simeq0.942\pm0.014$, quantifying the normalization mismatch under those assumptions. We also discuss photon-loss and varying-$G$ interpretations: ordinary positive opacity cannot explain the negative central tilts $\varepsilon$ found for a $\Lambda$CDM background, while local gravity tests strongly constrain the illustrative unscreened varying-$G$ scenario.

hep-ph.title: Nonlinear Response of Schwarzschild Black Holes at Arbitrary Perturbative Order
hep-ph.author: Jiaqi Chen, Yu-Cun Xie
hep-ph.abstract: We establish recursive integration-by-parts identities that symbolically reduce the inhomogeneous solutions of the Regge-Wheeler-Zerilli equation to a small set of master integrals, yielding the nonlinear response kernels of Schwarzschild black holes at arbitrary perturbative order. We further derive a closed ODE system that enables rapid, accurate, and stable numerical evaluation of these master integrals. To demonstrate our result, we compute quadratic, cubic, and quartic quasinormal-mode coupling coefficients as special cases of the response kernels.

hep-lat.title: Mellin Moments of Proton Unpolarized GPDs at Nonzero Skewness from Lattice QCD with a Neural-Network Parametrization
hep-lat.author: Min-Huan Chu, Manuel Colaço, Krzysztof Cichy, Martha Constantinou, Arif Sarkar
hep-lat.abstract: We use lattice QCD to determine the generalized form factors (GFFs) entering the first four Mellin moments of the unpolarized isovector $u-d$ proton GPDs at nonzero skewness. The framework combines the polynomiality of the moments in the skewness $\xi$, with the short-distance expansion formalism, allowing the lattice-extracted reduced Ioffe-time distributions (ITDs) to be expressed in terms of GFFs. In order to extract the GFFs by fitting these relations to the lattice data, we parameterize each GFF with an artificial neural network (ANN) as a continuous function of the invariant momentum transfer squared $t$, which accommodates the kinematic coverage of the data in a flexible way. With this fit, we determine the fourteen GFFs that enter the first four Mellin moments, including the skewness-dependent GFFs. From the extracted GFFs, we obtain the quark total angular momentum of the isovector combination, $J^{u-d}=0.296(11)(7)$ in the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme at $\mu=2~\mathrm{GeV}$, in agreement with previous lattice determinations based on nonlocal operators and with a smaller total uncertainty. We also determine the impact-parameter distributions of the first three Mellin moments in an unpolarized and in a transversely polarized proton. We finally identify and discuss the principal systematic uncertainties which enter this extraction, and the challenges specific to the nonzero-skewness regime.

hep-lat.title: Progress on meson-glueball mixing in lattice gauge theories coupled to fermions in multiple representations
hep-lat.author: Nuno Brito, Ed Bennett, Deog Ki Hong, Jong-Wan Lee, C.-J. David Lin, Biagio Lucini, Maurizio Piai, Davide Vadacchino, Fabian Zierler
hep-lat.abstract: We present preliminary results from our numerical lattice investigation of the low-lying flavour-singlet bound states in the ${\rm Sp}(4)$ gauge theory coupled to fermions transforming in the fundamental and two-index antisymmetric representations. We use the Wilson gauge action and Wilson fermions. We employ the generalized eigenvalue problem (GEVP) method with a basis of smeared glueball and meson interpolating operators. We analyse two high-statistics ensembles with the same lattice coupling and different fermion mass. We study both the scalar and pseudoscalar states. We observe the first evidence for meson-glueball mixing in this theory. We improve upon previous determinations of the energy eigenstates and mixing angles in the flavour-singlet pseudoscalar sector.

hep-lat.title: Quark TMDPDFs from Large to Small $x$: A Unified Description of CSS, DGLAP, and Small-$x$ Double Logarithms
hep-lat.author: Swagato Mukherjee, Vladimir V. Skokov, Andrey Tarasov, Shaswat Tiwari
hep-lat.abstract: We extend the full-kinematic background-field construction developed for gluon transverse-momentum dependent parton distribution functions (TMDPDFs) in Mukherjee et al. [Phys. Rev. D 109, 034035 (2024)] to quark TMDPDFs, providing a common framework for their large- and small-$x$ dynamics. We compute the leading-power quark TMD beam function at next-to-leading order using the background-field method. The background fields retain both longitudinal and transverse momenta, with neither collinear nor eikonal ordering imposed. We distinguish the renormalization scales that define the TMD operator from the factorization scales that separate its perturbative and non-perturbative modes. With standard TMD renormalization, the quark TMDPDF obeys Collins-Soper-Sterman (CSS) evolution, while the lower-scale separation is organized directly in terms of background-field TMD operators. We refer to this full-kinematic construction as the MSTT scheme. In the MSTT scheme, the leading term of the resulting operator expansion reproduces both the Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) logarithm and the small-$x$ double logarithm in the appropriate limits, while retaining parts of the higher-twist and sub-eikonal corrections. We also formulate a rapidity-only scheme for quark TMDPDFs with distinct renormalization and factorization cutoffs. We derive its evolution equation, which reduces to DGLAP evolution in the collinear limit and to double-logarithmic quark evolution at small $x$, and establish its matching to the MSTT and standard TMD schemes.

hep-lat.title: Digital Quantum Simulation of Dynamics in Interacting Fields
hep-lat.author: Zhiyao Li
hep-lat.abstract: Matter under extreme conditions behaves as a non-equilibrium, strongly-interacting quantum system. Such systems are in the non-perturbative regime of quantum chromodynamics (QCD), where their time evolution is classically intractable. Quantum computing offers a promising alternative, but present-day devices are limited in qubit count and circuit depth, so efficient formulations and algorithms are key to scaling toward experimentally relevant QCD simulations. A scalable framework is established for simulating energy loss and hadronization in 1+1-dimensional SU(2) lattice gauge theory, in which a heavy quark traverses a lattice of light quarks. Classical lattice QCD methods are translated into physics-informed circuits to prepare the interacting ground state. The evolution is run on IBM's quantum processor ibm_pittsburgh, where the charge distribution and energy loss are measured. A further study develops the quantum simulation of the fully gauge-fixed SU(2) Hamiltonian in a mixed basis, a formulation that is expected to remain efficient at all gauge couplings. Digitizing the continuous gauge fields with as few as three qubits per plaquette reproduces low-energy observables with $10^{-3}$ precision. Scaling to larger systems is limited by resource overhead, which motivates truncations that preserve the relevant observables. Sequency Hierarchy Truncation (SeqHT) exploits the hierarchy in basis-operator contributions. Demonstrated on the adiabatic preparation of the $\lambda\phi^4$ ground state on ibm_sherbrooke, SeqHT reduces circuit depth by ~30%, suppressing hardware noise in the extracted observables. All simulations in this dissertation are validated on quantum hardware against classical benchmarks. These studies advance quantum simulations of real-time QCD dynamics.

hep-lat.title: The Standard Model on a finite bosonic lattice with continuum Weyl fermions
hep-lat.author: Stephen D.H. Hsu
hep-lat.abstract: We investigate a formulation of the Standard Model in which gauge and Higgs fields are regulated on a finite lattice, while quarks and leptons remain continuum Weyl fermions. This preserves the familiar continuum description of anomalies, spectral flow, and fermion zero modes, without requiring a finite-dimensional discretization of chiral fermions. The Standard Model's anomaly cancellation permits a gauge-invariant definition of the chiral fermion determinant. Yukawa interactions are included in the full fermion determinant using a gauge-covariant cutoff that acts on the interaction vertices rather than the fermion propagator. We show that removing this cutoff requires only the local subtractions expected from one-loop power counting, and construct a consistent complex fermion weight, including in topologically nontrivial backgrounds. At fixed bosonic lattice spacing and finite spacetime volume, the resulting bosonic functional integral is finite and exactly gauge invariant under the stated smoothness conditions. The construction provides a finite-regulator Standard Model formulation retaining the physical structure of continuum chiral fermions. Appendix F.5 establishes reflection positivity for a variant reconstruction at zero Yukawa coupling and zero theta. The bosonic continuum limit remains open.

hep-lat.title: Magnetic monopoles produced by first-order phase transition
hep-lat.author: Yuefeng Di, Ligong Bian, Rong-Gen Cai
hep-lat.abstract: We present the first 3D lattice simulations of magnetic monopole production from a first-order phase transition, using the Press-Ryden-Spergel method, capturing the subsequent annihilation stage and the entry into the scaling regime in an expanding universe. We establish the quantitative relationship between the initial bubble number and the residual monopole abundance, and calculate the magnetic field and gravitational wave power spectra sourced by monopole dynamics. Crucially, we find that the magnetic field spectrum displays a steep $k^{-5}$ decline beyond the monopole size $w_M$, whereas the peak of the gravitational wave spectrum aligns with the scale of the mean monopole separation $d_M$, governed by $k^3$ and $k^{-3}$ scalings on the low- and high-wavenumber sides of the peak, respectively. However, since the resulting magnetic field strength is excluded by blazar observations, magnetic monopoles cannot be the origin of primordial cosmic magnetic fields. Finally, we determine the allowed monopole mass under the constraints of the Parker bound ($m_M\lesssim2.18\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{GeV}$) and dark matter abundance ($m_M\lesssim1.58\times10^{12}\,\mathrm{GeV}$).

hep-th.title: Non-Geometric Heterotic Vacua from Type II$_0$ Loci
hep-th.author: Christian Aoufia, Giacomo Maggiorotti, Max Wiesner
hep-th.abstract: We determine 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ heterotic string backgrounds dual to Type IIB string theory compactified on Calabi--Yau threefolds containing a type II$_0$ locus in their complex structure moduli space. While previous work only established the existence of such a duality frame, we concretely identify the heterotic theories dual to one- and two-parameter models exhibiting such loci, yielding novel instances of Type IIB--heterotic duality. To establish the correspondence, we first match the massless $\mathcal{N}=2$ spectrum, which uniquely fixes the heterotic data. We then recover the light spectrum of BPS D3-branes wrapping cycles on the Type IIB side from the heterotic perspective, and finally match the duality groups governing the global structure of the vector multiplet moduli space. All resulting heterotic theories are genuinely lower-dimensional, as they do not admit a decompactification limit to ten dimensions in their hypermultiplet moduli space. We identify two classes of duals. In the first, the heterotic string is compactified on a geometric K3 with a standard gauge bundle, demonstrating explicitly that type II$_0$ loci admit a consistent description as weakly coupled heterotic strings. In the second, the heterotic string background is given by a string-scale K3 and is hence non-geometric and genuinely four-dimensional. In this case, directly establishing supersymmetry would require control over all perturbative and non-perturbative $\alpha'$ corrections. Here, the duality to Type IIB is most powerful, as it establishes the existence of new consistent, supersymmetric, and anomaly-free heterotic compactifications beyond the reach of conventional geometric methods. Finally, the Type IIB realization of the two-parameter models reveals that four-dimensional heterotic compactifications admit smooth transitions involving the nucleation of NS5-branes.

hep-th.title: De Sitter Observers and an Effective Field Theory of Horizon Edge Modes
hep-th.author: James Bonifacio, Kurt Hinterbichler, Y.T. Albert Law, Varun Lochab
hep-th.abstract: We show that choosing a test observer in $dS_D$, specified by the framed embedding of their horizon $S^{D-2}$, spontaneously breaks the de Sitter and internal sphere isometries to diagonal rotations. We identify gravitational edge modes, described by low diffeomorphism jet fluctuations near the horizon sphere, as the associated Goldstone modes. We construct their membrane-like effective theory, organized in a small-gradient expansion. We find a class of nonlinear actions that at the quadratic order reproduce the edge-mode spectrum previously found in the one-loop gravitational $S^D$ path integral.

hep-th.title: Quasinormal-mode stability bounds in gravitational EFT: resolvability, predictivity, and positivity
hep-th.author: Leonardo Juliano, Enrico Trincherini
hep-th.abstract: It has been proposed that consistency limits how slowly black holes can ring down in extensions of General Relativity: effective-field-theory (EFT) corrections may lengthen the decay time of a quasinormal mode by at most about one oscillation period, $\Re[\omega_{\rm GR}]\,\delta\tau\lesssim1$. We argue that, under standard power counting, this condition yields no new, model-independent constraint on gravitational EFTs. First, its motivation does not extend straightforwardly to black holes: the inverse oscillation frequency is not a universal, detector-independent uncertainty in the damping time of a classical waveform. Our main argument, however, rests on eikonal power counting alone. The decay-time shift grows with the angular momentum $\ell$ of the mode, but so does the weight of higher-derivative operators. When curvature and derivatives are controlled by a single scale $\Lambda$, as in every known ultraviolet completion, the EFT around a black hole of radius $r_s$ remains predictive up to $\ell\sim(r_s\Lambda)^2$, and the shift becomes of order one only there, where an infinite tower of operators contributes at the same order. A resolvable shift within the predictive regime requires either large numerical coefficients or a two-scale power counting, which has no known ultraviolet completion. In both cases the quartic-curvature operators dominate, and the condition coincides parametrically with the positivity bounds that flat-space graviton amplitudes impose under standard assumptions on the ultraviolet completion. Only in scalar--tensor theories could the two-scale window probe beyond positivity, and then at most one family of dimension-ten operators. The axial sector of Einstein--dilaton--Gauss--Bonnet gravity and Einstein--Maxwell theory illustrate these results.

hep-th.title: Twisted Correlators from Harmonic Superspace
hep-th.author: Dennis le Plat, Torben Skrzypek
hep-th.abstract: We establish a harmonic superspace formulation for $\mathcal N=2$ orbifolds of $\mathcal N=4$ super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory. We account for the orbifold projection by introducing topological defect lines to the planar supergraphs of $\mathcal N=4$ SYM. These twist lines are sourced by twisted sector operators, transparent to vector multiplets but generate orbifold phases when crossed by bifundamental hypermultiplet fields. This formalism establishes a refinement of the orbifold inheritance principle at supergraph level. As a direct application, we compute leading twist-dependent corrections to BPS two- and three-point functions, finding agreement with localisation results in extremal cases and generating new data for non-extremal correlators. We further map these corrections to finite-size effects in the twisted hexagon formalism. This opens a path towards an all-order integrability prescription of orbifold structure constants.

hep-th.title: de Sitter Gluon Correlators in Momentum Space
hep-th.author: Melvyn Nabavi, Guilherme L. Pimentel, Facundo Rost, Marcelo dos Santos, Jaroslav Trnka
hep-th.abstract: We show a new diagrammatic representation of tree-level wavefunction coefficients for gluons in four-dimensional de Sitter space at any multiplicity. Its ``disc diagrams" make the cutting rule manifest, while the remaining contact term is fixed by the absence of folded singularities. We determine this term for configurations with zero, one and two negative-helicity gluons. It simplifies as more gluons share a helicity, and it vanishes for all-plus. We illustrate the expansion at four and five points, attach explicit results up to eight points all-plus, and relate it to Grassmannian residues.

hep-th.title: Orientifold and Integrability: $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super-Yang-Mills on $\mathbb{RP}^4$
hep-th.author: Joao Caetano, Shota Komatsu, Paolo Soresina, Anders Wallberg
hep-th.abstract: We study planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory (SYM) on the real projective space $\mathbb{RP}^4$ using integrability, holography and supersymmetric localization, and discuss its relation to orientifolds in string theory. We show that the integrability of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM is preserved when combining the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ involution defining $\mathbb{RP}^4$ with the action of the charge conjugation of the SU$(N)$ gauge group. We demonstrate this by calculating one-point functions of non-BPS single-trace operators in various subsectors at weak coupling, which can be mapped to overlaps between energy eigenstates and crosscap states in integrable spin chains. The results exhibit a parity selection rule, a hallmark of integrability, and are given in terms of a ratio of determinants. Building on these results, we conjecture a closed formula for general single-trace operators. We further provide evidence that this construction is holographically dual to a probe orientifold O1-plane in $\text{AdS}_5\times \text{S}^5$ by constructing the corresponding worldsheet crosscap states in the pp-wave limit. Finally, we use supersymmetric localization to compute one-point functions of half-BPS operators exactly at finite $g_{\rm YM}$ and $N$. The computation reduces to two-dimensional Yang-Mills theory on $\mathbb{RP}^2$ twisted by charge conjugation and leads to a matrix integral of a Wishart-Laguerre type. In the planar limit, the exact result interpolates between the weak-coupling gauge-theory result, the strong-coupling supergravity prediction for the orientifold, and the worldsheet crosscap in the pp-wave limit.

hep-th.title: Can componentwise D7-tadpole cancellation yield a chiral Standard Model? A no-go for smooth O7$^{-}$ orientifolds
hep-th.author: Mudit Jain
hep-th.abstract: We study a componentwise prescription for D7-tadpole cancellation that includes, as a special case, the local cancellation used in several moduli-stabilisation constructions. We work in smooth Type IIB Calabi--Yau orientifolds with O7$^{-}$ components of pairwise distinct divisor classes. For each component class $[R_i]$, eight covering-space D7-branes are distributed among smooth irreducible representatives of that class in an orientifold-compatible way. Each component sector may therefore contain several orthogonal, unitary, or symplectic parent factors. We show that these configurations cannot supply the chiral Standard Model through their perturbative D7 spectrum. Without symplectic factors, the entire parent algebra of each component sector embeds into $\mathfrak{so}(8)$ and cannot contain commuting color and weak-isospin subalgebras. Disjointness excludes massless fermions connecting different component sectors, so quark-doublet fermions are absent. Configurations containing symplectic factors require a separate argument: massless hypercharge, together with the same disjointness, forces the net quark-doublet chirality to vanish. Both arguments allow admissible D7 gauge backgrounds and diagonal gauge embeddings, with no restriction on $h^{1,1}_{-}(X)$. We also give a geometric condition under which the tadpole forces purely local cancellation. For a specified finite set of allowed D7 support classes, a separate test identifies component sectors in which the tadpole forces componentwise cancellation. We discuss applications to toric constructions and axion potentials.

hep-th.title: Circling in on correlation functions in $\mathcal{N}=2$ orbifold theories
hep-th.author: Dennis le Plat, Torben Skrzypek
hep-th.abstract: We review the harmonic superspace formalism for 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ theories and apply it to orbifolds of $\mathcal N=4$ Super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory. These theories have a remarkably similar description to $\mathcal N=4$ SYM, but their planar supergraphs feature topological twist lines which generate phases when intersecting bifundamental hypermultiplet propagators. These cause twisted sector BPS correlators to depend on the coupling $g$. Twisted Coulomb-branch operators of length $L$ receive a leading perturbative contribution to their two-point function at order $\mathcal{O}(g^{2L})$ from a supergraph involving a wrapped hypermultiplet circle. After performing the complete $D$-algebra, we show that the supergraph reduces to the universal conformal period $W_L=\binom{2L}{L}\zeta(2L-1)$. We extend this analysis to multiple nested hypermultiplet circles and show that they reproduce a series of higher-order terms in the exact localisation result. A subsequent evaluation of leading contributions to BPS three-point correlators again shows complete agreement with localisation results in extremal case and generates new perturbative data in the non-extremal case. The latter involves one untwisted BPS descendant, which contains physical hypermultiplet fields and can therefore connect directly to the twist-dependent hypermultiplet circle. This reduces the suppression in $g$, resulting in a contribution $4 g^{2(\ell+1)} W_{\ell+1}$ controlled by a bridge length $\ell$ rather than by an external operator length $L\geq\ell$. These examples demonstrate the feasibility of harmonic superspace calculations in orbifold theories and point to various future applications in the context of non-BPS correlators, integrability and marginal deformations.

hep-th.title: The 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model
hep-th.author: John F. Dawson
hep-th.abstract: We develop the 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model with a central extension, starting from Wigner's theorem and the supertranslation group. The unitary representations of the group leads to the SUSY algebra of the generators and an extension of the group to include a central charge $Z$. We then derive a general boson/fermion mass-degeneracy theorem and construct the covariant derivative and a candidate action realizing this algebra, first for the vacuum ($Z=0$) sector and then for $Z\neq0$, where the central extension's own coordinate $\xi$ is treated explicitly. Compactifying $\xi$ gives a Kaluza--Klein tower of massive multiplets with quantized central charge, while the kink survives intact as the tower's zero mode, saturating the general BPS bound $M\geq|Z|$ derived along the way. This is a pedagogical re-derivation, aimed at a reader's first encounter with these ideas, not a new result.

hep-th.title: "Massive" Conformal Field Theories and application to Nambu-Goto string
hep-th.author: Yuri Makeenko
hep-th.abstract: I describe the recent progress in understanding diffeomorphism invariant two-dimensional theories with dimensionful parameters which have nevertheless traceless improved energy-momentum tensor and turn out to be conformal invariant. An example is the Liouville theory with the additional four-derivative terms arising from the Nambu-Goto string and telling apart the Nambu-Goto and Polyakov strings. Its exact solution in embedding dimension d=4 is consistent in contrast to the Polyakov string and described by the (4,3) unitary minimal model. Talk at Irina Aref'eva Conference "Perspective Directions in Quantum Field Theory and Superstrings", Moscow 12-17 October 2026.

hep-th.title: Scale Anomaly in Supersymmetric Quantum Electrodynamics: Ward Identities, Supersymmetry Breaking, and Decoupling
hep-th.author: A. Yu. Petrov, A. R. Vieira
hep-th.abstract: We study the breaking of the scale symmetry both within classical and quantum frameworks in the supersymmetric quantum electrodynamics (SQED) by applying a four-dimensional regularization that preserves supersymmetry. At the classical level, scale symmetry is shown to be broken by mass terms. At the quantum level, it is demonstrated to be broken by a term proportional to the SQED beta function in the massless limit. It is also shown how this anomaly manifests itself in the low- and high-energy limits and how the Appelquist-Carazzone theorem reproduces the usual quantum electrodynamics result in the limit of heavy selectrons.

hep-th.title: Stable and causal frames for BDNK hydrodynamics
hep-th.author: Jay Armas
hep-th.abstract: We establish the existence of families of linearly stable and causal Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) frames for arbitrary equation of state and set of physical transport coefficients. By developing a method based on simplification of Routh-Hurwitz criteria and telegrapher factorisation of polynomials, we provide six concrete examples of such families, three of which admit conformal limits, for both neutral and charged fluids. These frames have adjustable characteristic speeds and can serve as a starting point for numerical implementations of relativistic hydrodynamics in various settings. In the process we uncover a map between stable and causal frames in neutral fluids and stable and causal frames in charged fluids. We also develop an AI research protocol that can be used to search for such frames in any hydrodynamic theory.

hep-th.title: The Standard Model on a finite bosonic lattice with continuum Weyl fermions
hep-th.author: Stephen D.H. Hsu
hep-th.abstract: We investigate a formulation of the Standard Model in which gauge and Higgs fields are regulated on a finite lattice, while quarks and leptons remain continuum Weyl fermions. This preserves the familiar continuum description of anomalies, spectral flow, and fermion zero modes, without requiring a finite-dimensional discretization of chiral fermions. The Standard Model's anomaly cancellation permits a gauge-invariant definition of the chiral fermion determinant. Yukawa interactions are included in the full fermion determinant using a gauge-covariant cutoff that acts on the interaction vertices rather than the fermion propagator. We show that removing this cutoff requires only the local subtractions expected from one-loop power counting, and construct a consistent complex fermion weight, including in topologically nontrivial backgrounds. At fixed bosonic lattice spacing and finite spacetime volume, the resulting bosonic functional integral is finite and exactly gauge invariant under the stated smoothness conditions. The construction provides a finite-regulator Standard Model formulation retaining the physical structure of continuum chiral fermions. Appendix F.5 establishes reflection positivity for a variant reconstruction at zero Yukawa coupling and zero theta. The bosonic continuum limit remains open.

hep-th.title: Extended Local Infrared Cutoff for the Holographic Density
hep-th.author: L. N. Granda
hep-th.abstract: We propose an extended local infrared cutoff for the holographic density that leads to linear cosmological equations and gives exact analytical solutions. The model allows to remove the residual matter and radiation-like terms of the local construction based on $H$ and $\dot{H}$, resulting in a clear separation between the standard cosmological fluids and the holographic sector. The homogeneous solution generates characteristic modes that give rise to different cosmological behaviors. The extension includes derivatives up to third order, where two of the characteristic modes can modify the pre-recombination expansion and reduce the sound horizon while remaining subdominant at BBN. A slightly phantom mode provides an additional late-time geometrical freedom that can further increase the CMB-compatible value of $H_0$. Optimizations using BAO constraints yield values of $H_0$ in the approximate range $70.5-72.4\ {\rm km\;s^{-1}\;Mpc^{-1}}$.

hep-th.title: Graviphoton mixing with KK modes in the 2D effective theory of charged black holes
hep-th.author: Yoshihiko Abe, Tetsutaro Higaki, Yu Miyauchi
hep-th.abstract: We study the effects of massive Kaluza--Klein modes on the two-dimensional low-energy effective theory obtained by the $S^2$ reduction of four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory on a Reissner--Nordström black hole background. We retain the first excited ($l=1$) Maxwell Kaluza--Klein modes in addition to the massless sector. The background electric flux mixes the Maxwell Kaluza--Klein scalars with the graviphotons, and tree-level exchange of the massive scalars generates a correction to the graviphoton kinetic term proportional to the square of the black hole charge. Within the leading local approximation, we also perturbatively evaluate the one-loop correction to the graviphoton kinetic term and find no dependence on the black hole charge. We find that near extremality, the charge-dependent tree-level correction becomes parametrically comparable to the classical graviphoton kinetic term.

hep-th.title: 8-type electric flux tube solutions in SU(3) gauge theory
hep-th.author: Jude Pereira
hep-th.abstract: We consider electric flux tube solutions in SU(3) gauge theory with scalar fields in the fundamental representation, for an electric field in the $\lambda_8$ direction (8-type). In temporal gauge, the 3-type electric field rotates within a single SU(2) subgroup at one frequency, whereas the 8-type electric field necessarily rotates within three SU(2) subgroups with at least two different frequencies. We construct the homogeneous 8-type electric field with three scalar fields and show that two scalar fields are sufficient only on a one-parameter family of gauge field backgrounds. Like the 3-type field, the homogeneous 8-type field is immune to decay through Schwinger pair production of gauge bosons. We then construct an 8-type electric string solution in temporal gauge. Its electric field is of 8-type on the string axis and, unlike the 3-type string, the string is only net color neutral, which results in a weak radial electric field.

hep-th.title: Fermion-Number Variation for Several Coupling Schemes in an $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Chiral Soliton Background
hep-th.author: Nobuyuki Sawado, Shintaro Yamamoto
hep-th.abstract: When topological solitons are coupled to fermions, they often induce a nontrivial fermion number. In the chiral quark soliton model (CQSM), this phenomenon underlies the identification of soliton topology with baryon number. However, whether this topology--fermion-number correspondence is determined solely by soliton topology or also depends on the fermion--soliton coupling scheme remains unclear. In this paper, we investigate this question by comparing several coupling schemes to the same $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ chiral soliton background. To treat the corresponding Dirac Hamiltonians within a common framework, we evaluate the variation of the regularized fermion-number along a model-parameter space. For the standard chiral Yukawa coupling of the CQSM, this variation reproduces the topological charge $Q$ associated with $\pi_3(\mathrm{SU}(N))$. The same result is obtained for an axial-vector coupling, whereas the fermion number variation vanishes for a vector coupling, despite the nontrivial topology of the chiral soliton background. These results provide an explicit example in which soliton topology alone does not determine the fermionic response; the topology--fermion-number correspondence also depends on how the background field is coupled to fermions.

hep-th.title: Scalar-scalar-graviton vertex from Asymptotic Safety
hep-th.author: Tim Eckert, Benjamin Knorr
hep-th.abstract: The unitarity and causality properties of asymptotically safe quantum gravity are still unsettled. Scattering amplitudes provide a direct test, but their computation requires fully momentum-dependent correlation functions. In this light, we compute the full scalar-scalar-graviton vertex from Asymptotic Safety within a mostly analytic approximation. Qualitatively, we find the expected logarithmic branch-cut structure, and we correctly recover the double-eikonal soft divergences predicted by Weinberg's soft theorem. Quantitatively, we find that non-minimal operators are generally as important as the minimal vertex stemming from the scalar kinetic term.

hep-th.title: Carrollian Symmetries and Dynamical Entropy
hep-th.author: Michael Imseis
hep-th.abstract: Carrollian geometry has recently emerged as the proper language to understand the geometry of null hypersurfaces from an intrinsic perspective. In this paper, we demonstrate that the Noether charge associated with the intrinsic conformal symmetry of Carrollian manifolds yields exactly the dynamical entropy formula recently proposed by Hollands, Wald and Zhang. This result follows directly from the requirement that the gravitational phase space induced on a finite distance null hypersurface be anomaly-free, in a covariant phase space sense. We then show that a linearized perturbation of this dynamical entropy charge, sourced by an external matter perturbation falling across the hypersurface, satisfies a physical process first law. Moreover, upon imposing the classical null energy condition, a linearized second law holds for the dynamical entropy. We then turn to a semi-classical generalization of this construction, where we argue that a notion of dynamical generalized entropy follows from considering perturbations sourced by external quantum matter. By imposing the quantum null energy condition (QNEC), we find a generalized second law for a linearized perturbation of the dynamical generalized entropy. Finally, we use our results to speculate on relations to the quantum focusing conjecture.

hep-th.title: Random Euclidean CFT$_2$ from Triangulated dS$_3$ Gravity
hep-th.author: Ji-seong Chae
hep-th.abstract: We propose a random Euclidean CFT description of three-dimensional de Sitter gravity, with fixed central charge and primary spectrum but fluctuating operator product coefficients. Our construction starts from compact regions assembled from generalized hyperbolic tetrahedra. We analytically continue the gravitational amplitudes computed from these triangulations to de Sitter parameters and use them to infer OPE correlations. We recover matching normalized amplitudes from a complex Liouville cosmological wavefunction. A non-Gaussian fourth moment encodes the hyperbolic core volume in an oscillatory semiclassical phase. We construct the associated Lorentzian de Sitter spacetime and show that derivatives of this phase recover its boost holonomies. Its spacelike future boundary carries a positive-definite conformal metric, while the wavefunction obeys Euclidean conformal Ward identities. These relations connect the proposed OPE statistics to both the Euclidean boundary description and the Lorentzian bulk geometry. Integrating the absolute square of the cosmological wavefunction over boundary moduli gives cosmological observables. Their long-collar factorization reproduces the edge measure of the two-matrix model.

hep-th.title: A signature of the timelike singularity in holography
hep-th.author: Joydeep Chakravarty, Yoav Zigdon
hep-th.abstract: In the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence, we provide a simple observable, the imaginary part of the retarded Green's function, which captures the timelike singularity of a charged black brane. Solving wave equations of bulk fields with different spins outside the black brane, we calculate exponentially small contributions to retarded Green's functions in the dual CFT at large real frequency. These contributions admit an interpretation in terms of paths in an analytically continued classical black brane interior via a WKB approximation: they provide the complex time elapsed along null geodesics that reflect off the singularity, and incorporate the corresponding reflection coefficients.

hep-th.title: Dyonic black holes supporting nearly-black self-gravitating thin shells
hep-th.author: Shahar Hod
hep-th.abstract: It has recently been revealed that dyonic black-hole spacetimes of a quasitopological non-linear electrodynamic field theory may be characterized by discrete radial regions with the property $dg_{tt}(r)/dr=0$ in which spherically symmetric massive {\it test} shells (Dyson shells with negligible self-gravity) can be supported in static equilibrium states. In the present paper we prove that the dyonic spacetimes of the non-linear electrodynamic field theory may also be characterized by the presence of radial regions with the dimensionless property $d[r\cdot g_{tt}(r)]/dr\to0^+$ in which massive {\it self-gravitating} thin shells that are on the verge of becoming black holes can be supported in static equilibrium states. Intriguingly, it is proved that the discrete radii of these self-gravitating nearly-black Dyson shells are universal in the sense that they are independent of the masses of the central supporting dyonic compact objects.

hep-th.title: Liouvillian Non-Invertible Symmetry
hep-th.author: Ying-Cheng Yang, Jhen-Dong Lin, Yueh-Nan Chen
hep-th.abstract: Non-invertible symmetries extend conventional symmetries beyond group-like transformations and play an important role in quantum field theory and many-body physics. However, a general framework of non-invertible symmetries in open quantum systems is still lacking. Here, we formulate a general Liouville-space duality framework that extends Hilbert-space non-invertible dualities to open quantum systems. The resulting defect relates Liouvillians with dual Hamiltonian and dissipative parameters and becomes an exact symmetry at self-duality. We apply this framework to the periodic transverse-field Ising chain with two collective Lindblad channels exchanged by Kramers--Wannier (KW) duality. A strong $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry divides Liouville space into four parity sectors, while the defect acts nontrivially only in the even-even sector. At self-duality, the KW defect imposes a momentum-resolved selection rule on Liouvillian Jordan blocks. Modes with different Liouville momenta or KW-defect eigenvalues cannot form a common exceptional Jordan block. For a three-site chain, a global Rényi-2 KW asymmetry dynamically identifies the self-dual conditions. At the same time, the spectral structure exhibits both a semisimple degeneracy and a self-dual exceptional point with a perturbation-selective response. These results extend non-invertible dualities to Markovian quantum dynamics and establish a symmetry-based selection rule for Liouvillian Jordan structures.

hep-th.title: Learning Parameters of dRGT Black Holes in Nonlinear Electrodynamics with Neural Network Scenarios
hep-th.author: Adil Belhaj, Salah Eddine Ennadifi, Maryem Jemri
hep-th.abstract: Using machine learning methods, we present constraining parameter scenarios of AdS black holes in dRGT-like massive gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics. We first approach the photon sphere, the black hole shadow, and the energy emission rate with the help of high performance parallel computations. To corroborate such optical results, we develop a numerical framework to constrain the electric charge and the nonlinear electrodynamic parameter, for certain gravity regimes, via the shadow observations reported by the Even Horizon Telescope collaboration. Employing neural networks, we then examine the parameter regions of the black holes based on their consistency with EHT observations of M87$^*$, SgrA$^*_{\mathrm{VLTI}}$, and SgrA$^*_{\mathrm{Keck}}$, within the $1-\sigma$ and $2-\sigma$ confidence intervals. As a result, we find that the obtained constraints are consistent with the $SgrA^*_{\mathrm{VLTI}}$ empirical data.

hep-th.title: Gauge Field Fluctuations Protect the Higgs Vacuum When a Small Universe Begins
hep-th.author: Alan Zhang(1 and 2) ((1) Department of Physics and Astronomy, McMaster University, Hamilton, Canada, (2) Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics, Waterloo, Canada)
hep-th.abstract: The Standard Model Higgs quartic coupling $\lambda$ turns negative at high energies. We show that in a small periodic box with antiperiodic fermions, zero-point fluctuations of the constant gauge modes turn the Higgs zero mode into a resonance for $\lambda<0$, whose width falls exponentially in $|\lambda|^{-1/2}$. A box lasting $N$ light-crossing times keeps its vacuum with probability above $1/2$ for $\lambda>\lambda_c(N)$, which depends on $N$ only logarithmically.
